summary: The SMTP module today does a shallow ESMTP probe — banner, EHLO features (STARTTLS flag + AUTH mech string), VRFY, a single-shape open-relay envelope, RCPT/VRFY/EXPN user enum against ~15 canonical names, plus a cleartext posture check on 25/587. It never actually completes a STARTTLS handshake, never attempts AUTH (the `creds` parameter is dead), never fingerprints server implementation/version, never tests SMTP smuggling (CVE-2023-51764/-51765/-51766) or bypass-style relay strings, never probes XCLIENT/XFORWARD/ETRN/BDAT/PROXY, and — critically — feeds NOTHING into the engagement-wide cross-service caches (known_users, known_hostnames, known_domains, relay_targets) despite being a first-class producer of all four (VRFY/EXPN/RCPT literally yield usernames; banner/EHLO/Received/cert CN yield hostnames and domains; every SMTP host is itself a relay pivot).
existing_capabilities: Port-set: 25, 465 (implicit TLS), 587, 2525 with SMTP_SSL branch on 465
probe(): connect + EHLO, capture first banner line (200-char trunc)
Reads esmtp_features dict: exposes 'starttls' bool and raw 'auth' mech string
Open-relay test: RSET/MAIL FROM/RCPT TO external recipient (envelope only, no DATA), 250/251 = relay
enum_users(): iterates ~15 canonical local names via VRFY / EXPN / RCPT TO <u@localhost> with per-attempt RSET
Optional user wordlist via --wordlist merged onto the bundled list
Findings: open_relay (high, CWE-269/16), vrfy (low, CWE-200), user_enum (medium, CWE-200/203), cleartext-no-STARTTLS on 25/587 (low, CWE-319)
findings_to_vulns via svccommon; analyze() honors active/budget/progress; is_smtp gate on port+service

missing_capabilities.name: SMTP smuggling detection (CVE-2023-51764/-51765/-51766)
missing_capabilities.description: Never sends the LF-only or bare-CR DATA payload sequences that revealed differential end-of-DATA parsing across Postfix / Sendmail / Exim / Cisco Ironport. Sending a benign-looking test message with `<LF>.<LF>` vs `<CR><LF>.<CR><LF>` and observing whether the second envelope is accepted would flag SPF/DKIM-bypassing smuggling. This is the highest-value modern SMTP primitive and the module is silent on it.

missing_capabilities.name: Implementation + version fingerprint → CVE mapping
missing_capabilities.description: Banner line is captured but never parsed for Postfix/Exim/Sendmail/Exchange/Microsoft ESMTP/qmail/Zimbra/Postfix-XCLIENT/Ironport. No version regex. Missing CVE hooks: Exim <4.92 CVE-2019-10149 (`${run{}}` RCE), Exim <4.94.2 21Nails CVE-2020-28017..-28026, Exim <4.97.1 CVE-2024-39929 (MIME filter), Exchange CVE-2020-0688 / CVE-2021-26855 ProxyLogon / CVE-2021-34473 ProxyShell, Zimbra CVE-2022-27924, Sendmail wiz/debug, qmail-1.03 assorted.

missing_capabilities.name: AUTH mechanism deep-probe (RFC 4954)
missing_capabilities.description: Only reads the advertised `AUTH` line; never issues AUTH. Missing: (a) enumerate every advertised mech (PLAIN, LOGIN, CRAM-MD5, DIGEST-MD5, GSSAPI, NTLM, XOAUTH2, EXTERNAL, SCRAM-SHA-*); (b) flag AUTH offered BEFORE STARTTLS (RFC 4954 §4 violation, credential-in-cleartext); (c) flag deprecated CRAM-MD5/DIGEST-MD5 as offline-crackable; (d) attempt NTLM Type-1 → server returns Type-2 that leaks NetBIOS domain, hostname, DNS domain, OS build — free info-disclosure primitive.

missing_capabilities.name: AUTH LOGIN username-oracle enum
missing_capabilities.description: Many MTAs (Exchange notoriously) return distinguishable error codes/text for valid vs invalid usernames during AUTH LOGIN before password. This survives even when VRFY/EXPN/RCPT are all locked down. Not attempted.

missing_capabilities.name: STARTTLS handshake + cert introspection
missing_capabilities.description: Module reports 'starttls advertised' but never issues STARTTLS or completes the TLS handshake. Missing: TLS version/cipher, self-signed / expired / weak-CA, cert CN + SAN list (feeds known_hostnames and known_domains), SNI virtual-hosting behavior, and STARTTLS-response-injection plaintext-command-injection class bug (CVE-2011-0411 Postfix, similar smtpd bugs).

missing_capabilities.name: Full EHLO extension inventory
missing_capabilities.description: Only 'starttls' and 'auth' surface. RFC-registered extensions not enumerated: SIZE, PIPELINING, 8BITMIME, DSN, ENHANCEDSTATUSCODES, CHUNKING (BDAT), SMTPUTF8, ETRN, TURN, ATRN, XCLIENT, XFORWARD, PROXY, PRDR, BURL, VERP, EXPN. Each is a fingerprint and several are direct attack primitives (below).

missing_capabilities.name: XCLIENT source-address spoofing (Postfix)
missing_capabilities.description: If server advertises XCLIENT and accepts it from the scanner IP (i.e. scanner is in mynetworks), an unauthenticated attacker can overwrite client IP/hostname/HELO/SASL — trivially bypasses IP-based relay controls and forges Received headers. Never probed.

missing_capabilities.name: XFORWARD header spoofing
missing_capabilities.description: Sibling of XCLIENT for downstream Received/Received-SPF forgery through a relay. Not tested.

missing_capabilities.name: ETRN / TURN / ATRN queue-release + hosted-domain leak
missing_capabilities.description: ETRN <domain> replies distinguish `250 queuing started` (this MTA IS a secondary for domain) vs `458/459 not allowed`. Free enumeration of every domain this MTA is a backup MX for → seeds known_domains cross-service. TURN/ATRN if enabled = relay pivot.

missing_capabilities.name: Open-relay bypass matrix
missing_capabilities.description: Only one relay shape tested (`MAIL FROM:<external> RCPT TO:<external>`). Missing the classic bypass syntaxes that catch MTAs that block naive relay but still forward: percent-hack `user%victim.com@relay`, bang-path `victim.com!user@relay`, quoted `"user@victim.com"@relay`, source-route `<@relay:user@victim.com>`, IP-literal `user@[a.b.c.d]`, localpart-only + HELO spoof, MAIL FROM:<postmaster@self> RCPT TO:<external>, and null-sender relay `MAIL FROM:<>`. Each is a distinct finding.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 5321 §3.6.1 (source routes, deprecated but still accepted)

missing_capabilities.name: BDAT / CHUNKING differential parsing
missing_capabilities.description: CHUNKING (RFC 3030) BDAT chunk-size vs DATA framing is a known SMTP-smuggling vector distinct from DATA-terminator smuggling. Not probed.

missing_capabilities.name: PROXY protocol acceptance
missing_capabilities.description: Postfix/Exim optionally speak HAProxy PROXY v1/v2 on 25/587. If open to the internet, attacker sends `PROXY TCP4 <spoofed> …` prefix and every downstream ACL / logging sees the spoofed source. Not detected.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: HAProxy PROXY v1/v2 spec; Postfix smtpd_upstream_proxy_protocol

missing_capabilities.name: EXPN list expansion of well-known aliases
missing_capabilities.description: enum_users runs EXPN per-user but does not target the high-yield aliases `all`, `everyone`, `staff`, `users`, `postmaster`, `abuse`, `mailer-daemon`, `root`, `wheel`, which historically expand to full user rosters in one shot. RFC 5321 §3.5.2 allows list expansion.

missing_capabilities.name: Callback / bounce-address verification abuse
missing_capabilities.description: Send `MAIL FROM:<victim@internal-domain>` `RCPT TO:<test@remote>` — many MTAs perform a callback to victim domain to verify sender exists, disclosing which internal addresses are considered legitimate senders and generating a scan-attributable NDR at the target. Not probed.

missing_capabilities.name: SPF / DKIM / DMARC posture for served domains
missing_capabilities.description: For every domain the MTA accepts inbound mail for (learned from RCPT TO on known_domains + ETRN + cert SANs), DNS-resolve SPF `v=spf1`, DMARC `_dmarc`, DKIM selectors. Absent/weak (`~all`, `p=none`) plus accepting MTA = spoofable-inbound finding. Purely passive DNS, high signal.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 7208 SPF, RFC 6376 DKIM, RFC 7489 DMARC

missing_capabilities.name: LMTP awareness
missing_capabilities.description: is_smtp() does not include 24 (LMTP), 2003, 2004. LMTP (RFC 2033) uses LHLO and often runs unauthenticated on internal nets — trivial local-delivery abuse and mailbox enumeration.

missing_capabilities.name: Submission (587) TLS-required enforcement
missing_capabilities.description: RFC 6409 §4.3 requires submission to demand TLS before AUTH. Module reports 'no starttls' but doesn't specifically flag AUTH-offered-on-587-without-TLS-required, which is the RFC violation.

missing_capabilities.name: Legacy Sendmail debug / wiz backdoor probe
missing_capabilities.description: `DEBUG` and `WIZ` (Sendmail <5.59) still occasionally appear on embedded gear. One-line docmd probe, high signal when it lands.

missing_capabilities.name: AUTH credential-spray with engagement creds
missing_capabilities.description: analyze() accepts `creds` but never uses it. When a spray-safe cred bundle exists and known_users has hits, attempt AUTH PLAIN/LOGIN over TLS with (user,pass) tuples for postmaster / admin / found-users. This is the credentialed pivot the module implies but never performs.

missing_capabilities.name: NTLM Type-2 domain/hostname leak via AUTH NTLM
missing_capabilities.description: When AUTH advertises NTLM (Exchange, IIS SMTP), sending a Type-1 message returns a Type-2 that leaks NetBIOS computer name, NetBIOS domain, DNS computer name, DNS domain, forest name, and OS version. Feeds known_hostnames + known_domains + AD recon. Free info-disclosure, no auth needed.

missing_capabilities.name: PIPELINING abuse fingerprint
missing_capabilities.description: Send multiple envelope commands in one flush; a server advertising PIPELINING but not enforcing per-command order boundaries is a smuggling precursor (Cisco Ironport CVE-2023-20075 family).

cross_service_wire_gaps: known_users: VRFY/EXPN/RCPT hits + any AUTH LOGIN oracle hits are literal engagement usernames but are never appended to the shared known_users cache (only surfaced inside this module's findings). Downstream sprayers (SSH, SMB, LDAP, HTTP-basic, RDP) do not see them.

known_hostnames: banner FQDN (line after `220 `), EHLO response server name, STARTTLS cert CN + SANs, Received: header hops (relay/enum test bounces), NTLM Type-2 DNS/NetBIOS names — none extracted, none fed to known_hostnames.

known_domains: every RCPT domain the server accepts (probeable), ETRN queue-release domain list, cert SAN domain suffixes, MAIL FROM callback verified sender domains, NTLM DNS/forest domain — none fed to known_domains.

relay_targets: an MTA is itself a relay/pivot node; open_relay=true or XCLIENT/PROXY/XFORWARD acceptance should register the host in relay_targets so ad/impacket modules can chain (e.g. SMTP → mail-based phishing pivot; XCLIENT → source-IP-laundering to internal services). Not wired.
known_hashes: AUTH CRAM-MD5 challenge captured from server, plus responses solicited during a credentialed test, are offline-crackable material — never captured or fed to known_hashes.
priority_gaps: P0 SMTP smuggling probe (CVE-2023-51764/-51765/-51766) — critical, current gap, no scanner in market catches it cleanly and it directly enables SPF/DKIM bypass.

P0 Wire VRFY/EXPN/RCPT + AUTH-LOGIN oracle hits into known_users, and banner/EHLO/cert/Received/NTLM leaks into known_hostnames + known_domains — the single highest-leverage change; every other service module benefits.
P0 Implementation/version fingerprint → CVE mapping for Exim (10149, 21Nails, 39929), Exchange (0688, ProxyLogon, ProxyShell), Zimbra (27924); banner is already captured, just needs parsing.
P1 XCLIENT / XFORWARD / PROXY-protocol acceptance probes — each is an unauth source-spoof primitive.
P1 STARTTLS handshake + cert introspection (feeds hostnames/domains, catches STARTTLS-injection class bugs, TLS-required-on-submission violation).
P1 AUTH mechanism deep-probe: AUTH-before-STARTTLS violation, NTLM Type-2 info-disclosure, CRAM-MD5/DIGEST-MD5 deprecation, plus wiring the currently-dead `creds` parameter into a spray step.
P1 Open-relay bypass matrix (percent-hack, bang-path, source-route, quoted, null-sender, IP-literal) — current single-shape test misses configured MTAs that still relay via legacy syntax.
P2 ETRN / EXPN-alias sweep — cheap, feeds known_domains + full user rosters in one shot.
P2 SPF/DMARC/DKIM check for every domain the MTA accepts inbound for — spoofable-inbound is a distinct finding class.
P2 LMTP port coverage (24, 2003, 2004) and BDAT/CHUNKING differential.
notes: Confirmed via `grep` that recce/core/known_users.py, known_hostnames.py, and known_domains.py contain zero references to `smtp`, banners, STARTTLS, or SMTP-derived tokens — the module truly produces nothing for the shared caches today, unlike pop3.py which explicitly documents seeding all three. The `creds` parameter in analyze() is accepted but never referenced in the module body — dead. `active` gates the probe loop but not any auth attempts (there are none). Tests only cover open_relay / vrfy / cleartext against a hand-rolled fake — no coverage for AUTH, STARTTLS negotiation, XCLIENT, ETRN, smuggling, fingerprint, or cross-service wiring.
